Verified empirically: `ExtendedData({'a':1,'b':[1,2,3]})` and `ExtendedData([1,2,3])` construct correctly with no double-init on current main. Deleted the 6 local branches after confirming supersession to leave nothing dangling.

decision: Fix root-cause CI lint failure on PR #49 by ignoring CPY/PLR0917 under ruff 0.16 and parenthesizing real ISC004 findings, rather than pinning ruff's version in tox.ini.
why: PR #49's 'Quality, docs, and build' check failed: tox's [testenv:lint] has an unpinned `deps = ruff>=0.8.0` floor (separate from the workspace's uv-locked ruff==0.15.22), so CI's tox-uv resolved fresh ruff==0.16.0 for lint only. ruff 0.16 newly activates CPY001 (missing copyright header, 130 hits) and PLR0917 (too-many-positional-args, 9 hits) under the project's `select = ["ALL"]`, and tightened ISC004 (unparenthesized implicit string concat in collection literals, 5 hits, all in packages/extended-data/tests/core/test_release_hygiene.py) neither of which existed/fired under 0.15.22. Considered and rejected pinning tox.ini's lint deps to `ruff>=0.15.22,<0.16`: that only defers the same class of break to whenever the workspace's own `ruff>=0.15.22` floor in pyproject.toml naturally resolves past 0.16 via `uv lock --upgrade`, and masks real newly-surfaced signal rather than triaging it. Instead: (1) added `CPY` to [tool.ruff.lint].ignore in both root pyproject.toml and the duplicated per-package packages/extended-data/pyproject.toml (discovered ruff resolves nested pyproject.toml [tool.ruff] tables per-file, so the workspace-root config alone does not govern files under packages/extended-data/ — root config only governs packages/pytest-extended-data/, which has no local [tool.ruff] table) — repo has zero copyright-header convention anywhere, so enforcing CPY would mean fabricating one from nothing, pure unrequested churn; (2) added PLR0917 to ignore in both files alongside its existing sibling PLR0913 (project already opts out of the whole pylint arg-count-nagging family: PLR0911/12/13/15); (3) fixed the 5 ISC004 findings for real by wrapping the implicit multi-line string concatenations in explicit parens in test_release_hygiene.py, since these were genuine (if harmless) ambiguity ruff correctly flagged and the fix is a trivial, safe, zero-behavior-change edit. Verified against both ruff 0.15.22 and 0.16.0 explicitly via `uv tool run --with ruff==0.16.0`: all checks pass on both. Did not run `ruff format` on the whole file — it revealed unrelated pre-existing format drift across the file (confirmed via `git checkout -- <file> && ruff format --check` before any edit) that predates this change and is out of scope; applied the two string-literal edits by hand instead so the diff stays minimal. Full suite: 802 passed both before and after.
resolves: CI failure on team-lead directive's cleanup PR (jbcom/extended-data#49)

decision: After merging PR#49, dispatched two independent review agents (code-reviewer against the PR#49 diff; general-purpose against overall repo health/drift) per the owner's mandatory-review-pass directive, then fixed every real finding in a follow-up PR (#51) instead of just reporting them.
why: code-reviewer verified the CPY/PLR0917/ISC004 fix was substantively correct (proved ISC004 edits ast-dump-identical before/after; proved PLR0917's underlying functions are called with a max of 2 positional args anywhere in the repo via AST scan of all 116 .py files, so ignoring it is not masking real call-site debt) but flagged the stated 'no copyright convention' CPY rationale as technically imprecise (LICENSE + package metadata already satisfy MIT's copyright-notice obligation; added an inline comment explaining this instead of leaving a bare ignore entry) and flagged that packages/extended-data/pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] duplicate of root's ignore list, now needing edits in two places, is itself the bug class recurring. The general-purpose audit independently found the SAME duplication problem plus two more real, already-drifted instances: packages/extended-data/pyproject.toml's [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths was narrowed to just "tests" (silently excluding pytest-extended-data/tests) and [tool.coverage.run] source was narrowed to just "extended_data" (dropping pytest_extended_data), both masked only by tox always invoking from repo root; plus a redundant but non-drifted [tool.mypy] duplicate. Both agents also independently confirmed tox.ini's `ruff>=0.8.0` unpinned lint-env floor (the actual mechanism behind PR#49's break) was still live and unaddressed. Fixed all of it in PR#51: collapsed packages/extended-data/pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] to `extend = "../../pyproject.toml"` (verified empirically that extend inheritance is load-bearing, not a silent no-op, by temporarily removing ANN from root's ignore and confirming 30 real ANN findings surfaced under packages/extended-data/ before restoring); deleted the drifted [tool.pytest.ini_options]/[tool.coverage.*] duplicates entirely (root's already cover the full workspace correctly) and the redundant [tool.mypy] duplicate; switched tox.ini's [testenv:lint] from `deps = ruff>=0.8.0` to `runner = uv-venv-lock-runner` (tox-uv's `uv sync --locked` mode) so the lint env always resolves the exact same uv.lock as every other `uv sync` invocation in the repo — verified `.tox/lint/bin/ruff --version` now reports 0.15.22 matching uv.lock exactly, vs. previously resolving a fresh 0.16.0 every run; this closes the drift class permanently since `uv sync --locked` fails hard if uv.lock and pyproject.toml ever disagree. Also independently verified packages/pytest-extended-data actually works as a real pytest plugin end-to-end (not just import-compile): built fresh wheels via `uv build`, installed them into a clean `uv` project, confirmed the pytest11 entry point auto-registers (shows in pytest's own `plugins:` banner) and exercised all its fixtures/assertion helpers via 6 out-of-tree tests, all passing. Full suite (802 tests) and `tox -e lint,typecheck,audit,examples,docs,build` (CI's exact invocation) verified green both before opening PR#51 and after it merged to main (f81cb20), with post-merge CI on main also confirmed fully green via fresh gh api checks.
resolves: owner's mandatory comprehensive-review-pass directive before reporting done on jbcom/extended-data
